problem.title: Design a 10B-Item Multimodal Joint-Embedding Search Engine

spark.summary: Architect a cross-modal search engine indexing 100M images, 750M video keyframes, and 500M text documents at 15,000 peak QPS with p95 < 200 ms, Recall@100 >= 0.92, and < 30s ingestion freshness.
spark.keyTakeaway: Decouple offline TensorRT SigLIP/ColPali ingestion from a tiered SQ8 DRAM HNSW + PQ64 NVMe DiskANN + BM25 scatter-gather path, fused via RRF (k=60) and reranked with 2-bit ColPali MaxSim.
spark.byteSummary:
Designing a planetary-scale multimodal search engine requires balancing three competing constraints: massive GPU encoding throughput for 30 fps video, terabyte-scale vector memory economics, and sub-200 ms p95 query latency across text, image, and video-region queries.

On the ingestion path, FFmpeg demuxers paired with PySceneDetect histogram deltas (> 0.30) and 64-bit pHash deduplication (Hamming >= 8) collapse 30 fps video into ~0.5 keyframes/sec before dynamic batching (B=128) on TensorRT FP16/BF16 SigLIP-So400M and ColPali GPU pools.

On the serving path, 850M 1150-D visual vectors (3.91 TB raw FP32) are tiered into a Hot DRAM HNSW+SQ8 cluster (1.8 TB provisioned DRAM, 8 ms) and a Warm NVMe DiskANN+PQ64 cluster (48 GB RAM + 3 TB NVMe, 25 ms), alongside a 500M-doc BM25 inverted index. Scatter-gather merges Top-200 lists via RRF (k=60), prefetches 7.2 MB of 2-bit quantized ColPali patches from NVMe for MaxSim reranking (42 ms), and collapses contiguous video keyframes within 5-second sliding windows.

learningJourney.title: Stage 1: Requirements Framing & Latency Budget Allocation
learningJourney.purpose: Establish corpus scale, 15,000 QPS traffic mix, and the 200 ms p95 end-to-end latency budget across retrieval stages.
learningJourney.explanation: The engine must index 100M images, 50M videos (750M keyframes), and 500M text documents with < 30s p95 ingestion freshness. At 15,000 peak QPS (60% text, 30% image, 10% video region), the 200 ms p95 budget allocates 35 ms to query encoding, 30 ms to parallel scatter-gather, 8 ms to RRF fusion, 42 ms to ColPali MaxSim NVMe reranking, 15 ms to temporal collapse, and 10 ms to metadata hydration.

sectionDiagram.title: 140 ms Nominal Critical Path Within 200 ms p95 Search SLO

cards.label: 60 ms Tail Buffer
cards.detail: Keeping nominal stages at 140 ms leaves 60 ms headroom for straggler shards and GC pauses under 1.5x peak load.

cards.label: 30s Freshness SLO
cards.detail: Streaming Kafka-to-TensorRT ingestion commits new keyframes into mutable HNSW delta segments within 30 seconds.

sectionDiagram.summary: Allocating explicit millisecond budgets across encoding, scatter-gather, MaxSim reranking, and temporal collapse protects the 200 ms p95 SLO.
sectionDiagram.caption: End-to-end 140 ms critical path budget leaving 60 ms headroom under the 200 ms p95 latency SLO.

learningJourney.title: Stage 2: Capacity Math & Memory Tiering (DRAM vs. NVMe)
learningJourney.purpose: Size Hot DRAM HNSW+SQ8, Warm NVMe DiskANN+PQ64, and ColPali SQ2 patch clusters for 850M visual vectors.
learningJourney.explanation: Uncompressed 1150-D FP32 embeddings for 850M visual items total 3.91 TB. Tier A applies SQ8 (1 byte/dim = 977.5 GB) plus HNSW M=16 graph links (108.8 GB), provisioned at 1.8 TB DRAM (15 x 128 GB nodes) with headroom. Tier B uses PQ64 (54.4 GB in-RAM codebooks + 1.03 TB on 3 TB NVMe), while ColPali SQ2 stores 1024 x 128-D patches for 50M pages in 1.84 TB across an 18 TB NVMe array.

sectionDiagram.title: 4-Tier Storage Footprint for 850M Visual Vectors & 50M Patch Grids

nodes.label: Tier D: ColPali SQ2 Patch Store

cards.label: 3x DRAM Safety Factor
cards.detail: Provisioning 1.8 TB DRAM for 1.09 TB raw SQ8+HNSW accommodates OS page cache, segment merges, and RF=2.

cards.label: 5x NVMe IOPS Headroom
cards.detail: 18 TB NVMe array for 1.84 TB ColPali SQ2 patches absorbs 15,000 QPS concurrent random 36 KB reads.

sectionDiagram.summary: Tiering SQ8 HNSW in DRAM, PQ64 DiskANN on NVMe, and SQ2 ColPali patches on high-IOPS NVMe avoids multi-terabyte FP32 DRAM costs.
sectionDiagram.caption: Capacity sizing across Hot DRAM HNSW+SQ8, Warm NVMe DiskANN+PQ64, BM25, and ColPali SQ2 NVMe tiers.

learningJourney.title: Stage 3: Typed gRPC Contracts & Hybrid Multimodal Payloads
learningJourney.purpose: Define strongly typed protobuf contracts supporting text, image-byte, and hybrid queries with filter pushdown.
learningJourney.explanation: SearchMultimodalRequest accepts a QueryModality enum (TEXT, IMAGE_BYTES, HYBRID_MULTIMODAL), optional text_query and image_query_bytes, VectorFilter predicates, enable_colpali_rerank, rerank_depth (default 200), and rrf_k_parameter (default 60.0). Responses return CandidateMatch records carrying dense, lexical, and late-interaction scores plus video timestamp_start_sec and timestamp_end_sec bounds.

sectionDiagram.title: MultimodalSearchEngine gRPC Contract & Score Provenance

cards.label: Score Provenance
cards.detail: Returning dense_score, lexical_score, and late_interaction_score enables offline NDCG debugging.

cards.label: Temporal Bounding
cards.detail: CandidateMatch returns timestamp_start_sec and timestamp_end_sec so video players seek directly to the matched clip.

sectionDiagram.summary: Typed protobuf contracts unify text, image, and hybrid search while exposing per-stage scores and video clip timestamps.
sectionDiagram.caption: gRPC request validation, execution controls, and multi-score CandidateMatch output with video timestamp bounds.

learningJourney.title: Stage 4: Video Keyframe Chunking & TensorRT Batch Inference
learningJourney.purpose: Process 30 fps video streams into deduplicated keyframes and saturate TensorRT FP16 GPU pools within 30s freshness.
learningJourney.explanation: An FFmpeg demuxer extracts YUV420 frames and computes Bhattacharyya HSV histogram deltas (> 0.30) followed by 64-bit pHash Hamming checks (>= 8), reducing 30 fps video to ~0.5 keyframes/sec. A dynamic batch assembler groups 128 keyframes per TensorRT FP16/BF16 batch on SigLIP-So400M and ColPali workers, committing vectors to HNSW, DiskANN, and BM25 within 30s.

sectionDiagram.title: 30 fps Demux -> pHash Dedupe -> Dynamic Batch TensorRT Inference

cards.label: TensorRT Throughput
cards.detail: FP16/BF16 dynamic batching (B=128) maximizes GPU Tensor Core occupancy while holding p95 ingestion < 30s.

cards.label: Idempotent Asset Writes
cards.detail: Deterministic asset_id + frame_index keys prevent duplicate index entries on worker retries.

sectionDiagram.summary: Scene-cut filtering, pHash deduplication, and TensorRT dynamic batching convert raw video into indexed vectors in under 30 seconds.
sectionDiagram.caption: FFmpeg, PySceneDetect, pHash, and TensorRT FP16 batching write keyframes to HNSW, DiskANN, and BM25 within 30s.

learningJourney.title: Stage 5: Scatter-Gather Query Routing & Semantic Cache
learningJourney.purpose: Serve 15,000 QPS with hedged shard fan-out, semantic query caching, and RRF (k=60) candidate fusion.
learningJourney.explanation: Incoming queries first probe a semantic cache for near-duplicate embeddings before fanning out in parallel across Hot HNSW+SQ8 shards, Warm DiskANN+PQ64 shards, and BM25 partitions. Hedged requests mitigate tail-shard stragglers, and the router merges Top-200 lists from each tier via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60) in ~8 ms.

sectionDiagram.title: Hedged Scatter-Gather Across Vector & Lexical Shards

cards.label: Tail-Latency Hedging
cards.detail: Issuing a backup read to a replica shard after 18 ms caps straggler impact at 15,000 QPS.

cards.label: Recall@100 >= 0.92
cards.detail: Combining dense visual recall with BM25 keyword recall hits >= 0.92 Recall@100.

sectionDiagram.summary: Semantic caching, hedged shard reads, and RRF fusion keep first-pass retrieval fast and resilient at 15,000 QPS.
sectionDiagram.caption: Query router checks semantic cache, fans out hedged reads to HNSW/DiskANN/BM25, and merges via RRF.

learningJourney.title: Stage 6: ColPali MaxSim Reranking & 5s Temporal Window Collapse
learningJourney.purpose: Execute 42 ms async NVMe MaxSim reranking and collapse adjacent video keyframes into coherent clip spans.
learningJourney.explanation: For the Top-200 RRF candidates, the reranker issues async NVMe reads totaling 7.2 MB (200 x 36 KB SQ2 patch grids) and computes MaxSim token-to-patch inner products in ~42 ms. Next, a 15 ms post-processor groups keyframes by video_id and collapses hits within a 5-second sliding window, selecting the highest-scoring frame and merging [t_start, t_end] bounds.

sectionDiagram.title: 7.2 MB Async NVMe MaxSim + 5-Second Video Window Deduplication

cards.label: Result Diversity
cards.detail: Collapsing 5-second windows prevents one video scene from monopolizing all Top-10 result slots.

cards.label: Bounded NVMe Bandwidth
cards.detail: At 7.2 MB/query, 15,000 QPS with 10% ColPali-reranked traffic stays well within NVMe array throughput.

sectionDiagram.summary: Async NVMe MaxSim reranking and 5-second temporal collapse deliver high-precision clip-level results within 57 ms.
sectionDiagram.caption: Top-200 SQ2 patch grids undergo MaxSim scoring and 5-second video window collapse into clip-level results.

learningJourney.title: Stage 7: Drift Governance, Backpressure & Graceful Degradation
learningJourney.purpose: Protect search availability under 1.5x load spikes and block misaligned encoder deployments via canary drift gates.
learningJourney.explanation: Under 1.5x peak QPS (> 22,500 QPS), adaptive load shedding disables Tier B DiskANN fan-out or narrows ColPali rerank_depth from 200 to 50 to keep p99 < 450 ms. Simultaneously, CI/CD blue-green encoder deployments evaluate mean cosine drift on 10,000 golden anchors and automatically abort if Delta > 0.03.

sectionDiagram.title: Adaptive Rerank Shedding & <= 0.03 Cosine Drift Canary Gate

cards.label: Graceful Degradation
cards.detail: Trimming rerank_depth from 200 to 50 cuts NVMe patch I/O by 75% during traffic surges.

cards.label: Zero Corrupt Shards
cards.detail: Enforcing Delta <= 0.03 stops misaligned model weights before they poison live HNSW indexes.

sectionDiagram.summary: Dynamic rerank shedding protects p99 < 450 ms under load spikes while golden-anchor drift gates prevent index corruption.
sectionDiagram.caption: QPS-aware rerank depth shedding and <= 0.03 cosine drift canary gates protect production search SLAs.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does Tier A (Hot DRAM) use SQ8 quantization (1 byte/dim) instead of FP32 or PQ64 for 850M 1150-D vectors?

options.text: SQ8 shrinks vector memory 4x (to ~977.5 GB) while keeping sub-10ms DRAM distance math and high Recall@100.
options.feedback: Correct. SQ8 fits the hot corpus in 1.8 TB provisioned DRAM with minimal recall loss compared to aggressive PQ64 compression.

options.text: SQ8 eliminates the need to build an HNSW graph.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Tier A still builds an HNSW graph (M=16, ~108.8 GB) over the SQ8 vectors.

options.text: SQ8 converts 1150-D vectors into 1024 visual patch tokens.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 1024 patch tokens belong to Tier D (ColPali SQ2), not Tier A.

options.text: SQ8 allows BM25 inverted indexes to run on GPUs.
options.feedback: Incorrect. BM25 runs in Tier C on NVMe-backed inverted lists.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: SQ8 compresses 1150-D FP32 vectors by 4x so the hot HNSW graph fits in 1.8 TB DRAM with < 10 ms recall.

knowledgeChecks.question: What happens if an ingestion pipeline skips the 64-bit pHash and histogram-delta gates on 30 fps video?

options.text: Recall@100 drops to zero because HNSW cannot index video frames.
options.feedback: Incorrect. HNSW can index the frames, but cost and index bloat explode.

options.text: GPU encoding cost and vector storage bloat by ~60x with near-duplicate static frames.
options.feedback: Correct. Collapsing 30 fps to ~0.5 keyframes/sec avoids 60x redundant GPU inference and duplicate index entries.

options.text: ColPali MaxSim switches from 2-bit to 32-bit quantization automatically.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Patch quantization is configured at storage time, independent of frame rate.

options.text: RRF fusion parameter k changes from 60 to 1.
options.feedback: Incorrect. RRF k=60 is a query-time fusion constant.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Without scene-cut and pHash deduplication, 30 fps video emits ~60x more frames than necessary, overwhelming GPU inference and index storage.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does the query pipeline apply a 5-second sliding temporal window collapse after ColPali MaxSim reranking?

options.text: To delete old keyframes from the Warm NVMe DiskANN index.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Temporal collapse is a query-time result deduplication step, not an index deletion.

options.text: To group adjacent keyframes from the same video into a single clip span [t_start, t_end] and preserve Top-K diversity.
options.feedback: Correct. Merging nearby keyframes from the same video_id prevents duplicate frames from crowding out other relevant videos.

options.text: To verify that encoder cosine drift stays below 0.03.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Cosine drift <= 0.03 is checked during CI/CD canary validation.

options.text: To convert BM25 scores into cosine similarity.
options.feedback: Incorrect. RRF already merges BM25 and dense ranks prior to MaxSim reranking.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Temporal window collapse merges contiguous keyframes within 5 seconds of each other into one clip result with [t_start, t_end] bounds.

beginner.summary: A multimodal search engine indexes images, video frames, and text in one shared vector space and uses fast filtering to return top matches in under 200 ms.
beginner.keyTakeaway: Filtering video down to unique keyframes and splitting hot vs. warm indexes keeps search fast and affordable.
beginner.byteSummary:
Searching across millions of photos, videos, and documents starts by turning each item into a list of numbers (an embedding) using AI encoders. For videos, we only keep frames where the scene actually changes.

When a user searches, the engine checks fast memory indexes and keyword indexes in parallel, combines the best matches, and returns the exact video timestamps or images.

intermediate.summary: Combine PySceneDetect + pHash video chunking, TensorRT SigLIP-So400M batching, SQ8 DRAM HNSW, PQ64 NVMe DiskANN, and BM25 with RRF (k=60) fusion.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: Tiering 850M visual vectors between SQ8 DRAM and PQ64 NVMe meets 15,000 QPS and < 200 ms p95 without 4 TB of raw FP32 RAM.
intermediate.byteSummary:
The ingestion pipeline collapses 30 fps video to ~0.5 keyframes/sec via histogram deltas and 64-bit pHash before dynamic TensorRT batching (B=128) to hit < 30s freshness.

On the query path, hedged scatter-gather queries Hot DRAM HNSW+SQ8, Warm NVMe DiskANN+PQ64, and BM25 in parallel, fusing Top-200 lists with RRF (k=60).

advanced.summary: Full 10B-scale architecture pairing SigLIP-So400M 1150-D recall with 2-bit ColPali MaxSim NVMe reranking (7.2 MB/query), 5s temporal collapse, and <= 0.03 drift canary gates.
advanced.keyTakeaway: Bounding ColPali MaxSim to Top-200 RRF candidates and shedding rerank_depth under 1.5x load spikes keeps p95 < 200 ms and p99 < 450 ms.
advanced.byteSummary:
To hit Recall@10 >= 0.88 on dense visual documents while serving 15,000 QPS, the router prefetches 200 2-bit quantized 1024-patch ColPali grids (36 KB/page = 7.2 MB/query) from an 18 TB NVMe array for 42 ms MaxSim reranking, followed by 5-second video window collapse.

Under 1.5x traffic spikes, adaptive shedding trims rerank_depth from 200 to 50, while a 10K golden-anchor canary gate aborts encoder rollouts if mean cosine drift exceeds 0.03.
